question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}_{xy}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${f}_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({f}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-\frac{{e}^{y}}{{x}^{2}}) \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{y}}{{x}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

To find ${f}_{yx}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${f}_{y}(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{yx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{y}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{{e}^{y}}{x}) \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{y}}{{x}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y)+{f}_{yx}(x,y) & =-\frac{{e}^{y}}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{{e}^{y}}{{x}^{2}}=-\frac{2{e}^{y}}{{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$
